decisions.rationale: The complete technical head directly attests thinking, whose three components are introduced.
GSUM supplies three. Part, components and of its own expand the organizational relation and are not separate source heads.
This first technical head introduces Conception as one thinking component; later repeated forms own the four conceive predicates and final conception recap separately.
First BZHI counts the four types. The later repeated BZHI after the list has no second printed four there and stays unbanked.
GZHI is the object of conception, before the example and four alternative conceptions.
This first example SEMS CAN owns living being after say. It is not reused for the explicit living-being object supplied again in the second English case.
The complete example construction is rendered say, supported by example/like reference material and the local example. It does not mean an utterance verb here.
Second SEMS CAN supplies the positive complement of the first conception.
This DU marks the conceived-as complement and owns the first as being. It is kept distinct from the later as introducing the fourth positive complement.
First complete verbal form owns conceive in the first case. The English infinitive and of are supplied verbal support.
Third SEMS CAN is the being rejected by the second conception: it owns living being in that case’s other-than complement, not the English repeated object.

The full inflected negative copula realizes other than in the conceived category. Exact MIN PAR has no HGM gloss; base MIN PA negative-copula material and the complete second-case syntax support the contrast. Something is English nominal support, not part of this head.
Second complete verbal form owns the second conceive, whose source object is understood from the earlier object and repeated explicitly in English.
Fourth SEMS CAN belongs to the nonliving object of the third conception and owns the being inside its something-other-than object phrase.
This complete negative copula defines the third-case object as other than a living being. The English something is nominal support, while MIN PA retains its full source syllables.
Fifth SEMS CAN is the third case’s negative complement, distinct from its preceding nonliving object.

Second inflected MIN PAR owns the third case’s other than complement. The predicate retains its full form and negative scope, without claiming a literal HGM other-than gloss for the missing exact inflection.
Third complete verbal form owns conceive of something other than a living being, not the fourth anaphoric this same thing case.
The DANG after the third case owns the English and introducing the fourth. Earlier list coordinators are expressed as semicolons and are left unbanked.
Sixth SEMS CAN supplies the fourth case’s positive complement. This same thing is an anaphoric restatement of the earlier nonliving object, not an exponent of this positive SEMS CAN.
Second DU owns as in the fourth conceived-as relation.
Fourth complete verbal form owns the final conceive of this same thing.
The final source noun owns conception in the summary of first/third versus second/fourth types.
The complete ordinal directly attests first in the final evaluation; it is not a member of the earlier four-count word.
This DANG joins the first and third types, with its own English and.
The complete ordinal directly attests third, not the earlier cardinal three components.

The whole attested adjectival expression directly has unmistaken. Its complete negative scope is retained as one lexical unit; no positive stem is split inside English unmistaken or assigned a separate unapproved subword.
The complete ordinal directly attests second in the mistaken pair.
This DANG separately joins second and fourth; it does not reuse the previous pair’s and.
The complete ordinal directly attests fourth, distinct from both earlier cardinal BZHI tokens.
The whole predicate directly attests mistaken and applies only to the second/fourth pair. Its bound terminal apostrophe-o is left outside, not split into a source-less English word.

omissions.english: a living being after the second conceive of; something; this same thing; here; types of
omissions.reason: The second English object restates the previously given living object; the fourth this same thing resumes the preceding nonliving object. Source positive SEMS CAN in the fourth case is its living-being complement, not this same thing. Something and summary support nominalize or clarify those relations without separate source nouns.
